channelTitle: The Silver Bridge fell at rush hour - 46 people died - was it a warning? - Part 2
hook: Part 2: December 15, 1967 - the Silver Bridge groaned once, then dropped into the icy Ohio River with seventy cars on it. And the Mothman was never seen again.
storyParts: At five in the afternoon the bridge was bumper to bumper. A single eyebar chain - one hidden crack - snapped, and forty-six people went into the freezing river. It remains one of America's worst bridge disasters.

Here is what chills people to this day: the sightings stopped the night the bridge fell. No red eyes, no wings, nothing. As if whatever it was came only to point at the disaster - and left once it happened.

Researchers have explanations - a misidentified sandhill crane, mass panic, cold-war paranoia. But the town built a twelve-foot statue of the thing anyway, standing guard downtown with polished red eyes.
Every September Point Pleasant holds a Mothman Festival - thousands of people come to celebrate the strangest guardian angel a town ever had. The fear became folklore, the folklore became identity.
So was it a monster, an omen, or a mass hallucination? After sixty years nobody knows - and maybe that is exactly why the story refuses to die.
cta: Do you think the Mothman was a warning or a threat? Grandma June reads every comment - tell me your theory.
moral: The scariest stories endure because they sit right on the line between warning and threat.
seriesTitle: The Mothman Warnings - Grandma June Stories
